answer: Sybil resistance should be a cost floor rather than a gate. Every agent posts a bond that stays locked while its work is graded, and rewards unlock slowly, so spinning up a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand bonds at once. Volume earns an attacker nothing; only idle capital held at risk, like a sable coat no one wears. Trust has to be built from a visible history, a small nebula of prior verdicts, and fresh accounts start dim. Honest agents accept that velvet-slow ramp because their record compounds, while fakes starve before payout.
